chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When God bestows a bounty upon His servant, He loves to see it upon him, because He is Beautiful and loves beauty.

key_terms.الجمال: Beauty — the quality God loves to see reflected in His creation
key_terms.جميل: Beautiful — one of the divine names/attributes (al-Jamil), meaning God possesses transcendent beauty
key_terms.نعمة: Bounty, favour, blessing — a gift from God

ai.seo_question: Why does Islam encourage showing God's blessings outwardly?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that when God grants a blessing to a person, He desires to see that blessing manifested visibly on them, grounding this in the divine attribute of beauty (al-Jamil). This hadith serves as a theological and ethical basis for manifesting God's blessings — particularly in dress, appearance, and livelihood — rather than concealing them out of false modesty. The teaching reflects the Quranic injunction (93:11) to speak of God's blessings.
